# minuta

> Divide time into pieces: pure functions over plain, deeply readonly `Period` data (`{ start, end, unit }`, `start` included and `end` excluded) of Temporal values: `PlainDate` for year to day, `ZonedDateTime` for hour to second. The unit rules are plain data ("units").

## Rules

- Two entries: `@aleksejdix/minuta` has every function; `@aleksejdix/minuta/temporal` has `temporalReady()`. Where the runtime has no Temporal, `await temporalReady()` first.
- The main entry is `withUnits(createUnits())`: weeks starting on Monday, moments in the runtime's zone, each date's own calendar. For other rules, `withUnits(createUnits({ locale, weekStartsOn, weekend, timeZone, calendar }))` returns every function with the same names; its `units` are the units passed in.
- Names follow Temporal: `round` takes Temporal's `smallestUnit`, `roundingIncrement` and `roundingMode`; `equals` and `compare` work like Temporal's; `toLocaleString` formats; `count` returns a number of units (`start.until(end)` gives a `Temporal.Duration`).
- No result is `undefined`, never `null` (`clamp` without overlap, `merge([])`, …).
- Invalid input throws `RangeError`; the message starts with one of the error codes below and says how to fix it.
- Nothing is mutated: every function returns new data.

## Error codes

- `INVALID_OPTION`: An option such as `step` or `maxPeriods` is not a positive whole number.
- `TOO_MANY_PERIODS`: `divideWith` would create more chunks than `maxPeriods` allows.
- `UNIT_NOT_SUPPORTED`: The `units` passed to a function have no spec for the requested unit.

## `@aleksejdix/minuta`

### `count`

```ts
count(source: Period, unit: Unit): number
```

How many complete `unit`s fit into a period, calendar- and DST-aware: a
number, where `start.until(end)` gives a `Temporal.Duration`.

```ts
count(day(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-10-08")), "hour"); // 24
count(month(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-02-01")), "day"); // 28
```

### `divide`

```ts
divide(source: Source, unit: Name, options?: DivideOptions): Chunks<Source, Name>
```

Split a period into chunks of `unit`, clipped to the period. Weeks start
on Monday.

```ts
divide(month(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-01")), "day"); // 31 day periods
divide(hour(Temporal.Now.zonedDateTimeISO()), "minute", { step: 15 }); // 4 periods
```

### `merge`

```ts
merge(periods: readonly Source[], unit?: Unit): Source | undefined
```

Merge periods of one kind into one spanning the earliest start to the
latest end. The result keeps `unit` (by default the first period's unit)
only when it is exactly one period of that unit; otherwise its unit is
`"custom"`.

```ts
merge([januaryFirstHalf, januarySecondHalf], "month"); // January, unit "month"
merge([january, march]); // Jan 1 – Apr 1, unit "custom"
merge([]); // undefined
```

### `next`

```ts
next(source: Source): Source
```

The next period of the same unit. Weeks start on Monday.

```ts
next(month(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-15"))); // April 2026
```

### `previous`

```ts
previous(source: Source): Source
```

The previous period of the same unit. Weeks start on Monday.

```ts
previous(month(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-15"))); // February 2026
```

### `round`

```ts
round(value: PlainDate, roundTo: RoundTo<DateUnit>): PlainDate
round(value: ZonedDateTime, roundTo: RoundTo): ZonedDateTime
round(value: PlainDate | ZonedDateTime, roundTo: RoundTo): PlainDate | ZonedDateTime
```

Round a date or a moment to a unit's boundary, like Temporal's `round()`
with the same options, extended to weeks, months, quarters and years.
With `roundingIncrement`, boundaries count from the start of the
enclosing unit (minutes from the hour, days from the month); weeks and
years from 1970.

```ts
round(Temporal.ZonedDateTime.from("2026-03-15T10:37[Europe/Zurich]"), { smallestUnit: "minute", roundingIncrement: 15 }); // 10:30
round(Temporal.ZonedDateTime.from("2026-03-15T10:37[Europe/Zurich]"), { smallestUnit: "day", roundingMode: "ceil" }); // Mar 16 00:00
round(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-18"), { smallestUnit: "week", roundingMode: "floor" }); // Monday 2026-03-16
round(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-18"), "month"); // 2026-04-01 (halfExpand)
```

### `shift`

```ts
shift(source: Source, steps: number): Source
```

Move a period by `steps` of its own unit; negative moves back.

```ts
shift(month(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-15")), 3); // June 2026
```

### `day`

```ts
day(value: TimeValue): DatePeriod
```

The day that contains `value`: its calendar date, a moment's in its own
zone.

```ts
day(Temporal.ZonedDateTime.from("2026-03-18T23:30[Asia/Tokyo]")); // 2026-03-18 up to 2026-03-19
```

### `hour`

```ts
hour(value: TimeValue): TimePeriod
```

The hour that contains `value`, in the moment's zone; a date is its first
hour in the runtime's zone.

```ts
hour(Temporal.ZonedDateTime.from("2026-03-18T10:30[Europe/Zurich]")); // 10:00 up to 11:00
```

### `minute`

```ts
minute(value: TimeValue): TimePeriod
```

The minute that contains `value`.

```ts
minute(Temporal.ZonedDateTime.from("2026-03-18T10:30:45[Europe/Zurich]")); // 10:30 up to 10:31
```

### `month`

```ts
month(value: TimeValue): DatePeriod
```

The month that contains `value`.

```ts
month(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-15")); // 2026-03-01 up to 2026-04-01
```

### `quarter`

```ts
quarter(value: TimeValue): DatePeriod
```

The quarter that contains `value`.

```ts
quarter(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-05-15")); // 2026-04-01 up to 2026-07-01
```

### `second`

```ts
second(value: TimeValue): TimePeriod
```

The second that contains `value`.

```ts
second(Temporal.ZonedDateTime.from("2026-03-18T10:30:45.5[Europe/Zurich]")); // 10:30:45 up to 10:30:46
```

### `week`

```ts
week(value: TimeValue): DatePeriod
```

The week that contains `value`, from Monday (ISO 8601). For another week
start, use `withUnits(createUnits({ weekStartsOn }))`.

```ts
week(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-18")); // Monday 2026-03-16 up to 2026-03-23
```

### `year`

```ts
year(value: TimeValue): DatePeriod
```

The year that contains `value`.

```ts
year(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-15")); // 2026-01-01 up to 2027-01-01
```

### `dayGrid`

```ts
dayGrid(value: TimeValue): DayGrid
```

The real hours of the day containing `value`: 23 on a spring-forward day,
25 on a fall-back day, 24 otherwise, each slot with the wall-clock hour it
starts in. The day lies in the zone of a moment passed in, else in the
runtime's zone.

```ts
const { periods, gapHour } = dayGrid(Temporal.ZonedDateTime.from("2024-03-10T12:00[America/New_York]"));
periods.length; // 23
gapHour; // 2
```

### `isWeekday`

```ts
isWeekday(source: Period): boolean
```

Whether every day the period touches is a working day: not Saturday or
Sunday (the units' `weekend` with `withUnits`).

```ts
isWeekday(day(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-18"))); // true (a Wednesday)
```

### `isWeekend`

```ts
isWeekend(source: Period): boolean
```

Whether every day the period touches is a Saturday or a Sunday (the units'
`weekend` with `withUnits`).

```ts
isWeekend(day(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-21"))); // true (a Saturday)
```

### `monthGrid`

```ts
monthGrid(value: TimeValue): MonthGrid
```

A stable month grid: 42 day periods (6 weeks) from the Monday of the week
that contains the first of the month.

```ts
monthGrid(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-15")).periods; // 42 days from Mon Feb 23
```

### `yearGrid`

```ts
yearGrid(value: TimeValue): YearGrid
```

A stable year grid: whole weeks, Monday first, from the week containing
the year's first day to the week containing its last.

```ts
yearGrid(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-06-01")).periods; // 53 week periods
```

### `clamp`

```ts
clamp(period: Period, bounds: Period): Period | undefined
```

Constrain a period to fit within bounds: the time the two share.

Returns undefined when they share no time, also when they only touch.
Next to a time period, a date period becomes moments in that period's
zone.

```ts
const selection = period(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-01-05"), Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-01-25"));
const allowed = period(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-01-10"), Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-01-20"));
clamp(selection, allowed);
// → { start: 2026-01-10, end: 2026-01-20, unit: "custom" }
```

### `compare`

```ts
compare(first: Period, second: Period): number
```

Order two periods by their start, then by their end, like Temporal's
`compare()`: a sort callback. Next to a time period, a date period becomes
moments in that period's zone.

```ts
[april, march].sort(compare); // [march, april]
compare(monday, week); // -1: the same start, the day ends first
```

### `contains`

```ts
contains(period: Period, target: Target): boolean
```

Whether a period contains a date, a moment or another period. `end` is
excluded: March does not contain April 1. A date counts as its whole day;
next to a time period, dates become moments in that period's zone.

```ts
contains(march, Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-20")); // true
contains(march, Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-04-01")); // false
```

### `equals`

```ts
equals(first: Period, second: Period): boolean
```

Whether two periods are identical, like Temporal's `equals()`: the same
unit and the same start and end, calendar and time zone included. For
"in the same week", use `same`.

```ts
equals(month(today), month(today)); // true
equals(month(today), period(march1, april1)); // false: a month and a custom period
```

### `gap`

```ts
gap(first: Period, second: Period): Period | undefined
```

The time between two periods: from where the earlier one ends to where
the later one starts. Order does not matter. For a date, pass its day:
`day(date)`.

```ts
gap(day(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-02")), day(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-05")));
// { start: 2026-03-03, end: 2026-03-05, unit: "custom" }: Mar 3 and 4
gap(day(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-02")), day(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-03"))); // undefined: they touch
```

### `overlaps`

```ts
overlaps(first: Period, second: Period): boolean
```

Whether two periods share any time. Periods that only touch (one ends
where the other starts) do not overlap. Next to a time period, a date
period becomes moments in that period's zone.

```ts
overlaps(march, april); // false: they touch
overlaps(march, week(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-31"))); // true
```

### `period`

```ts
period(start: PlainDate, end: PlainDate): DatePeriod
period(start: ZonedDateTime, end: ZonedDateTime): TimePeriod
period(start: PlainDate | ZonedDateTime, end: PlainDate | ZonedDateTime): DatePeriod | TimePeriod
```

The period from `start` (included) to `end` (excluded), unit `"custom"`. Equal
values make an empty period; an end before the start is an error, as
nothing is swapped behind your back.

```ts
period(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-01-01"), Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-04-01"));
// { start: 2026-01-01, end: 2026-04-01, unit: "custom" }: January to March
```

### `toLocaleString`

```ts
toLocaleString(period: Period, locales?: string | readonly string[], options: DisplayOptions = {}): string
```

A period as locale-aware text, like Temporal's `toLocaleString()`, in the
format of its unit: the month and year for a month, a weekday and a day
for a day, a range for weeks and custom periods (shared parts collapsed by
`Intl.DateTimeFormat#formatRange`; a date period shows its last day, not
its exclusive end). For a month as a range, format `period(month.start,
month.end)`. The same text everywhere: on native Temporal and the
polyfill, on a server and in the browser.

```ts
toLocaleString(march, "de-CH"); // "März 2026"
toLocaleString(day, "en-US"); // "March 15, 2026"
toLocaleString(day, "en-US", { weekday: "short" }); // "Sun"
toLocaleString(week, "ja-JP"); // "2026/03/09～2026/03/15"
toLocaleString(period(march.start, march.end), "de-CH"); // "1.–31. März 2026"
```

### `createUnits`

```ts
createUnits(options: UnitsOptions = {}): AllUnits
```

Unit specs for every unit, computed with the TC39 Temporal API: date
units on `PlainDate`, time units on `ZonedDateTime`. Pass the result to
`withUnits`, `calendar`, `intervals` or any `…With` function. Weeks
start on Monday unless `weekStartsOn` says otherwise (`"sunday"` …
`"saturday"`, or 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday); `weekend` sets
the days `isWeekend` counts (Saturday and Sunday unless set); `locale`
takes both from a locale's week (`Intl.Locale#getWeekInfo`); `timeZone`
is where dates become moments; `calendar` the calendar dates are read in. Where the runtime has no Temporal,
`await temporalReady()` first.

```ts
import { createUnits, withUnits } from "@aleksejdix/minuta/core";

const time = withUnits(createUnits({ timeZone: "UTC", weekStartsOn: "sunday" }));
time.week(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-18")); // [Mar 15, Mar 22)

createUnits({ locale: "ar-EG" }).weekend; // [5, 6]: Friday and Saturday
```

### `UnitsOptions`

```ts
type UnitsOptions = WeekOptions &
  Readonly<{
    /**
     * IANA time zone that dates become moments in, e.g. when a day is
     * divided into hours: `"UTC"`, `"Europe/Zurich"`. Default: the runtime's.
     */
    timeZone?: string | undefined;
    /**
     * Temporal calendar every date is read in, e.g. `"hebrew"`,
     * `"islamic-umalqura"`, `"persian"`. Default: each date keeps its own
     * calendar (ISO 8601 for dates made from moments).
     */
    calendar?: string | undefined;
  }>;
```

Options of `createUnits`: the week, the weekend and the time zone.

### `MinutaError`

Codes at the start of the messages of errors minuta throws.

### `MinutaErrorCode`

```ts
type MinutaErrorCode = (typeof MinutaError)[keyof typeof MinutaError];
```

One of the {@link MinutaError} codes.

### `withUnits`

```ts
withUnits(units: Units): Minuta
```

Bind every function to `units`: the same names as the main entry, with
your week start, weekend, time zone, calendar or locale.

```ts
import { createUnits, month, withUnits } from "@aleksejdix/minuta";

const time = withUnits(createUnits({ locale: "he-IL", calendar: "hebrew" }));
time.month(Temporal.Now.plainDateISO()); // this Hebrew month
time.monthGrid(Temporal.Now.plainDateISO()); // its Sunday-first weeks
time.units; // the units passed in
```

### `Minuta`

```ts
type Minuta = UnitPeriods & Functions;
```

Every function and a member per unit, bound to one set of units.

### `Round`

```ts
type Round = {
  (value: PlainDate, roundTo: RoundTo<DateUnit>): PlainDate;
  (value: ZonedDateTime, roundTo: RoundTo): ZonedDateTime;
};
```

`round`: a date to date units, a moment to any unit.

### `Chunks`

```ts
type Chunks<
  Source extends Period,
  Name extends Unit,
> = Source extends DatePeriod
  ? Name extends DateUnit
    ? DatePeriod[]
    : TimePeriod[]
  : TimePeriod[];
```

The chunks a division makes: date periods when a date period is divided
by a date unit, time periods otherwise.

### `DivideOptions`

```ts
type DivideOptions = Readonly<{
  /** Maximum number of periods before throwing. Default: 100,000. */
  maxPeriods?: number | undefined;
  /** How many units each chunk spans. Default: 1. */
  step?: number | undefined;
}>;
```

Options for `divide` / `divideWith`.

### `RoundOptions`

```ts
type RoundOptions<Name extends Unit = Unit> = Readonly<{
  /** How many units lie between boundaries. Default: 1. */
  roundingIncrement?: number | undefined;
  /** Temporal's rounding mode. Default: `"halfExpand"` (nearest, ties up). */
  roundingMode?: RoundingMode | undefined;
  /** The unit whose boundaries to round to */
  smallestUnit: Name;
}>;
```

Options for `round`, named like Temporal's `round()` options.

### `RoundTo`

```ts
type RoundTo<Name extends Unit = Unit> = Name | RoundOptions<Name>;
```

A unit, or the options with its `smallestUnit`, like Temporal's `round()`.

### `RoundingMode`

```ts
type RoundingMode = NonNullable<
  Temporal.RoundingOptions<"day">["roundingMode"]
>;
```

How `round` picks the boundary: Temporal's rounding modes.

### `WeekOptions`

```ts
type WeekOptions = Readonly<{
  /**
   * Locale whose week to follow: its first day and its weekend, as
   * `Intl.Locale#getWeekInfo` gives them (`"en-US"` starts on Sunday,
   * `"ar-EG"` on Saturday with a Friday–Saturday weekend). `weekStartsOn`
   * and `weekend` win over it. Default: none, the ISO 8601 week.
   */
  locale?: string | undefined;
  /** First day of the week. Default: `"monday"` (ISO 8601), or the locale's. */
  weekStartsOn?: Weekday | WeekdayNumber | undefined;
  /** Days that `isWeekend` counts as weekend. Default: `["saturday", "sunday"]`, or the locale's. */
  weekend?: readonly (Weekday | WeekdayNumber)[] | undefined;
}>;
```

Week options of `createUnits`.

### `Weekday`

```ts
type Weekday =
  | "friday"
  | "monday"
  | "saturday"
  | "sunday"
  | "thursday"
  | "tuesday"
  | "wednesday";
```

A day of the week by name.

### `WeekdayNumber`

```ts
type WeekdayNumber =
  | typeof SUNDAY
  | typeof MONDAY
  | typeof TUESDAY
  | typeof WEDNESDAY
  | typeof THURSDAY
  | typeof FRIDAY
  | typeof SATURDAY;
```

A day of the week as a number: 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday.

### `DayGrid`

```ts
type DayGrid = Readonly<{
  /** The hour slots of the day */
  periods: readonly HourSlot[];
  /** Wall-clock hour that doesn't exist due to spring forward, or undefined */
  gapHour: number | undefined;
  /** Wall-clock hour that occurs twice due to fall back, or undefined */
  ambiguousHour: number | undefined;
}>;
```

The real hours of a day: 23, 24 or 25 slots, with the skipped and the
repeated wall-clock hour.

### `HourSlot`

```ts
type HourSlot = TimePeriod &
  Readonly<{
    /** Wall-clock hour (0-23) the slot starts in, in the day's zone */
    hour: number;
  }>;
```

One real hour of a day, labelled with its wall-clock hour.

### `MonthGrid`

```ts
type MonthGrid = Readonly<{
  monthStart: PlainDate;
  /** The 42 day periods, row by row */
  periods: readonly DatePeriod[];
  /** The weekday the grid starts on, 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday */
  weekStartsOn: number;
}>;
```

A 42-day month grid (`periods`), the month's first day and the week start
the grid was built with.

### `YearGrid`

```ts
type YearGrid = Readonly<{
  /** The week periods covering the year */
  periods: readonly DatePeriod[];
  /** The weekday the grid starts on, 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday */
  weekStartsOn: number;
  yearStart: PlainDate;
}>;
```

The whole weeks covering a year (`periods`), the year's first day and the
week start the grid was built with.

### `AllUnits`

```ts
type AllUnits = Readonly<{ [Name in BuiltInUnit]: SpecOf<Name> }> &
  Readonly<{ timeZone: string }> &
  Settings;
```

A spec for every built-in unit, as `createUnits()` returns. Add specs of
your own units next to them: `Object.assign({ fortnight }, createUnits())`.

### `BuiltInUnit`

```ts
type BuiltInUnit =
  | "day"
  | "hour"
  | "minute"
  | "month"
  | "quarter"
  | "second"
  | "week"
  | "year";
```

The units every set of units provides. Units added to `UnitRegistry` come
with your own spec, so they are not part of `AllUnits`.

### `DatePeriod`

```ts
type DatePeriod = Readonly<{
  end: PlainDate;
  start: PlainDate;
  unit: DateUnit | "custom";
}>;
```

A span of calendar dates, `start` included and `end` excluded: March 2026
is `[2026-03-01, 2026-04-01)`. No time zone: a day is a date, so clock
changes cannot move it.

### `DateSpec`

```ts
type DateSpec = Readonly<{
  /** Marks a spec of calendar dates */
  kind: "date";
  add: (date: PlainDate, amount: number) => PlainDate;
  diff: (from: PlainDate, to: PlainDate) => number;
  startOf: (date: PlainDate) => PlainDate;
}>;
```

How one date unit behaves on calendar dates — plain data.

- startOf: the first date of the unit containing `date`
- add(date, n): the date `n` units later (negative: earlier)
- diff(from, to): the number of complete units from `from` to `to`,
  truncated toward zero: the largest `n` with `add(from, n) <= to` (for
  an earlier `to`, the smallest `n` with `add(from, n) >= to`)

### `DateUnit`

```ts
type DateUnit = {
  [Name in Unit]: UnitRegistry[Name] extends "date" ? Name : never;
}[Unit];
```

The units made of calendar dates: `"year"` … `"day"`, and your own.

### `Period`

```ts
type Period = DatePeriod | TimePeriod;
```

The primitive: every time range is a Period. Plain, deeply readonly data,
`start` included and `end` excluded.

`periodWith(units, value, "month")` creates one aligned to a unit,
`period(start, end)` a custom one.

### `PeriodOf`

```ts
type PeriodOf<Name extends Unit> = Name extends DateUnit
  ? DatePeriod
  : TimePeriod;
```

The period a unit makes: a `DatePeriod` for date units, else a `TimePeriod`.

### `PlainDate`

```ts
type PlainDate = Readonly<Temporal.PlainDate>;
```

A calendar date, read-only.

### `Settings`

```ts
type Settings = Readonly<{
  /**
   * IANA time zone that dates become moments in, e.g. when a day is divided
   * into hours. Default: the runtime's.
   */
  timeZone?: string | undefined;
  /** First day of the `week` spec, 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday. Default: Monday. */
  weekStartsOn?: WeekdayNumber | undefined;
  /** Weekend days, 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday. Default: Saturday and Sunday. */
  weekend?: readonly WeekdayNumber[] | undefined;
}>;
```

Settings that travel with the unit specs.

### `SpecOf`

```ts
type SpecOf<Name extends Unit> = Name extends DateUnit ? DateSpec : TimeSpec;
```

The spec of a unit: a `DateSpec` for date units, else a `TimeSpec`.

### `TimePeriod`

```ts
type TimePeriod = Readonly<{
  end: ZonedDateTime;
  start: ZonedDateTime;
  unit: TimeUnit | "custom";
}>;
```

A span of moments in one time zone, `start` included and `end` excluded:
the hour from 13:00 is `[13:00, 14:00)`.

### `TimeSpec`

```ts
type TimeSpec = Readonly<{
  /** Marks a spec of moments */
  kind: "time";
  add: (date: ZonedDateTime, amount: number) => ZonedDateTime;
  diff: (from: ZonedDateTime, to: ZonedDateTime) => number;
  startOf: (date: ZonedDateTime) => ZonedDateTime;
}>;
```

How one time unit behaves on moments, with the same contract as
`DateSpec`. Results stay in the zone of the value passed in.

### `TimeUnit`

```ts
type TimeUnit = {
  [Name in Unit]: UnitRegistry[Name] extends "time" ? Name : never;
}[Unit];
```

The units made of moments: `"hour"`, `"minute"`, `"second"`, and your own.

### `TimeValue`

```ts
type TimeValue = PlainDate | ZonedDateTime;
```

A value a period can be made from: a date or a moment, the two kinds a
period is made of. Date units read its calendar date; time units its
moment, a date's start of day in the units' time zone. No `Instant` or
`PlainDateTime`: give it a zone with Temporal, so none is guessed.

### `Unit`

```ts
type Unit = keyof UnitRegistry;
```

A unit name: `"year"`, `"quarter"`, `"month"`, `"week"`, `"day"`, `"hour"`,
`"minute"` or `"second"`, plus any unit added to `UnitRegistry`.

### `UnitRegistry`

Registry of unit names and their kind: `"date"` units (a year … a day)
are made of calendar dates, `"time"` units (an hour … a second) of
moments in a time zone. An interface so your code can add units through
module augmentation; the matching spec is passed as data in `Units`.

### `Units`

```ts
type Units = Readonly<{ [Name in Unit]?: SpecOf<Name> }> & Settings;
```

The unit specs available to unit-aware functions. Partial, so a bundle can
carry only the units it uses; `createUnits()` returns all, plus the
settings.

### `ZonedDateTime`

```ts
type ZonedDateTime = Readonly<Temporal.ZonedDateTime>;
```

A moment in a time zone, read-only.

## `@aleksejdix/minuta/temporal`

### `temporalReady`

```ts
temporalReady(): Promise<void>
```

Make Temporal available before minuta computes with it. Does nothing where
the runtime has Temporal (Chrome and Edge 144+, Firefox 139+, Node 26+);
elsewhere it loads `temporal-polyfill` in its own chunk and installs it
on `globalThis`. Await it once, before anything renders.

```ts
import { createUnits } from "@aleksejdix/minuta/core";
import { temporalReady } from "@aleksejdix/minuta/temporal";

await temporalReady();
const units = createUnits();
```
